sn22.56:1.5: Compare the “three rounds” of [sn56.11:9.1]() and the “eight rounds” of [an8.64:10.1]().
sn22.56:3.2: The “principal states” (_mahābhūtā_) are earth, water, fire, and air, corresponding to the modern concepts of solid, liquid, plasma, and gas. For the history of this term, see note on [mn28:4.2](). | “Derived” (_upādāya_) form is not explained in the suttas, but one passage indicates it includes “space” ([mn28:26.1]()). The Abhidhamma traditions explain it as including the objects of the senses, the subtle matter that receives sense impressions, and various other material phenomena.
sn22.56:3.4: For the topic of “fuel” (_āhāra_), here primarily meaning “food”, see  [sn12.11](), [sn12.63](), [mn9:10.2](), [sn47.42]().
sn22.56:5.2: _Kevala_ has the root meaning of “entire”, “exclusive”. For the Jains, _kevalī_ came to mean “one whose knowledge is entire”, i.e. an omniscient one. The Buddha used it to indicate one who has consummated the entire path.
